promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week ran about 53 miles against 38 planned, with a rest day run, an extra rep and a 20 mile long run. Feeling fine does not make that load safe to repeat, so next week drops to about 40 miles with one quality session and a 16 mile long run.

flags.detail: 53 mi against 38 planned, about 40 percent over plan and 43 percent over the week before. Next week goes back to about 40 mi.

flags.detail: they felt tight Sunday night after the 20 mi long run. Check them each morning this week and report it if they get worse.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
No, not at this size. Feeling fine on the day does not show that your legs have taken on a rise of about 43 percent in one week.

Next week drops to about 40 miles. After that, add no more than about 10 percent a week, and only once the planned week has felt right. If a planned rest day comes up, take it even when you feel good.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed
Sep 7 – 13 ran long on almost every day, and that matters more than any single session. Only the Friday rest day went as planned, and the Monday rest day was run. The table shows the gap.

| Measure | Planned or target | Done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distance | 38 mi | 53 mi |
| Long run | 15 mi | 20 mi |
| Wednesday hard reps | 3 at 8:00/mi | 4, the fourth at 7:55/mi |
| Easy share of time | 80 percent or more | 54 percent |

## Why the extra miles are the real issue
Feeling fine on a run does not show whether the legs can take a rise of this size in one week. Relative effort for the week was nearly double your three-week average, which is the usual sign that load has moved ahead of what the base can carry. Calves tight on Sunday night are a small early signal, and this is the right time to step back.

The right knee that bothered you in mid August settled by late August and has not come up since. A jump in load is when old areas tend to speak up, so note it in your check-in if it returns.

## Why Wednesday and Sunday both matter
The fourth rep came in faster than the 8:00/mi the session was built around, and most of that session was spent in zone 4. The Sunday run averaged 149 bpm with 88 percent of its time in zone 3, so it was not the easy run the plan called for. Those two sessions carry most of the extra hard time and explain the low easy share.

## How next week is built
Next week runs about 40 miles, a real step back from 53 but still a little above the 37 miles of the week before. The long run drops to 16 miles, roughly 2 hours 40 minutes at easy pace, so it stays the key session without the fatigue of 20 miles.

Wednesday keeps the same 8:00/mi threshold reps but stops at three. Sub 3:45 needs about 8:35/mi, so marathon-pace segments wait until the calves feel normal on the daily runs.

safetyCallouts.title: Tight calves after a big week.
safetyCallouts.body: Tight calves after a sharp jump in load are common, but watch them closely. If the pain grows from run to run, hurts when you walk, or swells, see a physio or doctor and stop running until they have checked you.
